topic.readerProblem: A buyer comparing Profound, Peec AI and Otterly.AI needs to know which of the three fits the number of prompts they must track, the engines their buyers use and their approval process, without guessing from reputation.
topic.connection: Positions a one-time AEOeye baseline as the step before buying a recurring tracker, and tells readers honestly that Otterly.AI, Peec AI and Profound are the right category when daily monitoring is needed.

assessment: The page is documentation-based and says so near the top: it uses each vendor's own pricing pages and documentation as checked on 2026-10-03, with no hands-on testing. It gives a prompt-count decision shortcut, one table of published prices, prompts, engines, trial and API/SSO terms with per-prompt costs computed from the published inputs, and a worked 40-question example. It makes no claim about data accuracy or output quality, notes Peec's trial length is not stated, reports Claude as Enterprise-only on Peec's page, and does not estimate Profound's brand price.

sources.supports: Lite $29 / Standard $189 / Premium $489 with 15 / 100 / 400 prompts, annual $25 / $160 / $422, four base engines, Claude add-on $29 / $109 / $439, Gemini and AI Mode add-ons, no extra prompts on Lite, API and MCP from Standard, Enterprise from 1,000 prompts with SSO, prompt research / brand visibility index / link citation analysis / GEO audit in every plan.

Starter / Pro / Advanced at $95 / $245 / $495 monthly and $80 / $205 / $420 annual (read from the page's own JavaScript data, since the dollar amounts are not in the served HTML), 50 / 150 / 350 prompts, three models, unlimited users, daily tracking, projects, multi-country and Looker Studio on Advanced, selectable models ChatGPT, AI Mode, AI Overviews, Copilot, Gemini, Naver AI, fourth-model add-on $35 / $85 / $165, Claude, Grok, DeepSeek, Qwen and Mistral shown only in the Enterprise column as API models, Enterprise API and SSO, a Start free trial button and no stated trial length.

Free Trial (50 prompts daily for 7 days on ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overviews) and custom Enterprise (up to nine engines, API, SSO/SAML and SOC 2, dedicated support); no monthly brand price listed; Agents and AI Marketer priced by credits.
Peec uses browser automation through the AI platforms' web interfaces rather than APIs, because API responses often differ from what users see.
Informational prompts often get answers that name no brands; commercial prompts reliably surface brands and are the core of most tracking; active prompts count toward the plan limit and run daily.
The GEO paper (Aggarwal et al., KDD 2024) reports GEO methods boosting visibility in generative engine responses by up to 40% in its test setup.
Definition of generative engine optimization as the practice of improving visibility in responses generated by generative AI systems.

checks: Writer (Sonnet): fetched Otterly's pricing page raw HTML with curl and Profound's pricing page raw HTML, and checked every plan, price, prompt count, engine and add-on figure used in the table against the page text.

Writer (Sonnet): Peec's dollar prices are not in its served HTML, so read them from the page's own JavaScript module (monthly and annual prices for the three brand plans and the three fourth-model add-on prices) and cross-checked prompt counts, model lists and the Enterprise-column API models against the rendered page text.

Writer (Sonnet): recomputed every per-prompt cost (plan price divided by prompts) and the 40-question worked example (40 x 3 x 30 = 3,600 answers at $95; 40 x 4 x 30 = 4,800 at $189) and labelled them as our arithmetic.
Writer (Sonnet): confirmed Peec's browser-automation statement and prompt-intent guidance in the raw text of docs.peec.ai pages, and the GEO paper's up-to-40% finding on arXiv, before citing them.

Writer (Sonnet): used first-hand AEOeye evidence only from the vendor study and evidence pack: robots.txt, /llms.txt and homepage JSON-LD observations for otterly.ai, peec.ai and tryprofound.com, plus AEOeye product facts (free 3-question ChatGPT audit, $29 one-time report, not a daily tracker); left out agency pricing because it is not in the served HTML.
